groups.instructions: Choose the correct option to complete each sentence.

questions.prompt: Between 2005 and 2015, the number of cinema visits ______ steadily.
questions.explanation: A finished period in the past (2005–2015) takes the past simple. The present perfect cannot be used with a completed past time frame.

questions.prompt: Since 2018, the price of electricity ______ by almost 40 per cent.
questions.explanation: 'Since' + a past point up to now takes the present perfect.

questions.prompt: By 2010, car ownership ______ its highest point and then began to decline.
questions.explanation: 'By' + a past year describes something completed before that time, so the past perfect is used.

questions.prompt: According to the forecast, the population of the city ______ 2 million by 2040.
questions.explanation: 'By' + a future year takes the future perfect: will have + past participle.

questions.prompt: The figure for online sales is expected ______ further over the next decade.
questions.explanation: 'be expected' is followed by the to-infinitive: is expected to increase.

questions.prompt: In 1990, only 12 per cent of households ______ a computer.
questions.explanation: A single past year takes the past simple. 'Own' is a state verb, so it is not normally used in the continuous form.

questions.prompt: The table shows how much water ______ in four countries in 2022.
questions.explanation: The verb 'shows' is present because the table exists now, but the data refers to 2022, so the past passive is needed.

questions.prompt: Unemployment remained stable for five years before it ______ sharply in 2009.
questions.explanation: A sequence of past events in chronological order uses the past simple.

groups.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct form of the verb in brackets. Write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS.

questions.prompt: Over the last ten years, the number of electric cars {{9}} (grow) dramatically.
questions.explanation: 'Over the last ten years' links the past to the present, so the present perfect is used.

questions.prompt: In 2000, spending on health care {{10}} (stand) at $300 per person.
questions.explanation: 'Stand at' is a common Task 1 verb for a value at one past time. Its past simple is irregular: stood.

questions.prompt: By the end of the period shown, rail use {{11}} (overtake) bus use.
questions.explanation: 'By the end of the period' (in the past) takes the past perfect.

questions.prompt: Coal production {{12}} (predict) to fall to almost zero by 2050.
questions.explanation: Predictions in the passive: subject + is predicted + to-infinitive.
